metadata.title: Unit Circle to Sine
metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.objective: Connect a point on the unit circle to the height of the sine curve.
metadata.learner: Knows right-triangle ratios; has not connected circular motion to sine.
misconceptions: Sine is only a triangle ratio
The sine value is the x-coordinate
expectedUnderstanding: sin theta is the y-coordinate (signed height) of the unit-circle point
the height is 0 at 0 and pi, 1 at pi/2, -1 at 3pi/2

primitives.text: height of the point = sin theta

checkpoints.title: Angle 0: height 0
checkpoints.body: The radius lies along the positive x-axis, so the point sits at y = 0 and the connector meets the sine axis at the baseline: sin 0 = 0. Drag the theta slider to set the angle; the sweep continues from the angle you choose.

checkpoints.title: Quarter turn: sin theta = 1
checkpoints.body: After a quarter turn the point is at the top of the circle. Its y-coordinate is 1, the connector has risen to the upper tick, and sine reads 1. Note that x is 0 here: sine takes the vertical coordinate, not the horizontal one.

checkpoints.title: Half turn: height 0 again
checkpoints.body: At theta = pi the point is at the far left with x = -1, but its height is back to 0. So sin pi = 0 even though the point is far from the origin. Sine reports signed height, not distance.

checkpoints.title: Below the axis: negative sine
checkpoints.body: Now the point is at the bottom, y = -1. The connector lies below the horizontal axis and the sine dot sits at the lower tick, so sin theta = -1. The sign of the height is part of the value.

checkpoints.title: One full turn
checkpoints.body: A full revolution brings theta back to 2pi, which lands on the same point as theta = 0, so sin 2pi = 0. Sine repeats with period 2pi. Drag the slider to any angle and check that the connector length always equals the size of the height.

narration.text: A radius sweeps around the unit circle; a connector carries the point's height across to the sine axis.
A quarter turn puts the point at the top: the height, and therefore sine, is 1.
At a half turn the height returns to 0 even though the point is at x = -1.
Below the axis the height is negative, so sine is negative.

fallback.text: A radius sweeps once around a unit circle from theta = 0 to 2pi in 12 seconds. A horizontal connector carries the point's height to a vertical axis on the right, where a dot marks the sine value. The height is 0 at theta = 0 and theta = pi, 1 at theta = pi/2, and -1 at theta = 3pi/2; the slider sets the starting angle.

accessibility.alt: Unit circle with a moving radius and point; a horizontal connector carries the point's height to a vertical axis where a dot marks sine, with ticks at plus one and minus one and labels for x and y.
